question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Early English Factories — Coastal Locations]
options: Masulipatnam — Located on the eastern coast (Coromandel Coast) of India
Surat — Located on the western coast (Gulf of Khambhat/Arabian Sea) of India
Hariharpur — Located in the Mahanadi delta region of Odisha (Eastern India)
Calcutta — Located on the Malabar Coast of southwestern India
wrong_fact: Calcutta is located on the eastern banks of the Hooghly River in Bengal (Eastern India), NOT on the Malabar Coast (which is the southwestern coast of India, modern Kerala).
explanation: Calcutta (now Kolkata) was established by the English (Job Charnock) in Bengal on the banks of the Hooghly River. The Malabar Coast is on the southwestern side of India, where early Portuguese and Dutch factories (like Cochin and Cannanore) were situated. Masulipatnam is on the Coromandel (southeastern) coast, Surat on the western coast (Gujarat), and Hariharpur/Balasore in Odisha (eastern coast).

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [English Presidency/Factory Headquarters — Fort Names & Locations]
options: Fort St. George — Located in Madras on the southeastern coast
Fort William — Located in Calcutta on the banks of the Hooghly River
Fort David — Located in Cuddalore, south of Madras on the Coromandel Coast
Fort St. Angelo — Located in Bombay on the western coast
wrong_fact: Fort St. Angelo is located in Kannur (Cannanore) in Kerala (Malabar Coast), built by the Portuguese, and was NOT the fort of Bombay on the western coast.
explanation: Fort St. George was the fortified settlement of the English East India Company in Madras (Chennai). Fort William was constructed in Calcutta (Kolkata). Fort St. David at Cuddalore was acquired by the British in 1690. Fort St. Angelo, however, is a famous Portuguese fort in Kannur (Kerala). The fort at Bombay was Bombay Castle, and the surrounding fortified area was known as Fort Bombay.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Early English Subordinate Factories — Administrative HQs]
options: Patna & Kasimbazar factories — Subordinate to the Presidency of Fort William (Calcutta)
Armagaon factory — Subordinate to Masulipatnam/Madras on the Coromandel Coast
Broach & Baroda factories — Subordinate to the Surat Presidency on the western coast
Balasore & Hariharpur factories — Subordinate directly to the Bombay Presidency from their inception
wrong_fact: Balasore and Hariharpur (established in 1633 in Odisha) were initially subordinate to the Madras agency (Fort St. George) and later to Bengal (Fort William), NOT to the Bombay Presidency on the opposite western coast.
explanation: Balasore and Hariharpur in Odisha (eastern coast) were established in 1633. Because of their geographic proximity to the eastern coast settlements, they were initially supervised by the Madras agency (Fort St. George) and later became part of the Bengal Agency/Presidency (Fort William). The Bombay Presidency had jurisdiction over western coast factories like Surat, Broach, Baroda, and Persian Gulf outposts.
